headline: The company AKASA has launched an AI system that it says can assign billing codes to hospital inpatient stays on its own, in under 90 seconds after the patient leaves.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a real product launch with named hospital users, but the accuracy claims come from the company.
importance_line: Hospital medical coders and the hospitals that employ them could see billing work shift to software, but the accuracy results are AKASA's own and the outside evaluators are not named.
summary: HIT Consultant reports that AKASA, a healthcare billing technology company, has launched an AI platform that it says turns hospital inpatient charts into billing codes without human intervention in under 90 seconds after discharge, a job AKASA says takes human coders 30 to 60 minutes per chart. AKASA says blinded third-party tests showed it matched or beat experienced human coders, but those results come from the company.
notes: Original outlet Fierce Healthcare blocked (HTTP 403); written from HIT Consultant, which largely repeats AKASA's announcement.
